subject: Concurrency windows and E2E latency benchmarks — post-call follow-up
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex@luminalabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Concurrency windows and E2E latency benchmarks — post-call follow-up

Hi Alex / Jordan —

Thanks for a productive call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared plan for the performance qualification: 

Summary of SLA targets you mentioned on the call:
- E2E latency (95th) for interactive streaming chat: <= 200 ms
- Steady-state QPS: ~120 requests/sec
- Typical tokens per request (avg): ~1,200 tokens
- Sustained concurrency target: ~600 concurrent active sessions (streaming-enabled)
- Short peaks: up to 4x steady-state for bursts lasting ~8–15s

Streaming specifics you called out:
- Client expects chunked responses with ~150–250ms chunk cadence
- Some requests include synchronous tool calls (external API hits) — these add variable tail time

Open clarifications we need from your side (please send before the bench run):
1) Canonical workload traces (ndjson or similar) with timestamps, tokens/request, and whether streaming/complete responses.
2) Percent of requests that are streaming vs non-streaming (estimate).
3) Any mandatory model variants (e.g., on-device model vs LLM-2.2) you require us to measure.

Redwood asks / bench prep from our side:
- We’ll provision a dedicated bench pool and run two passes: a guided throughput pass (replay of traces at scaled QPS) and an end-to-end streaming pass to validate chunk cadence and tail latencies.
- Tentative bench window: Mon 2028-07-11 10:00–14:00 PT. Please confirm availability.
- We’ll share a redwood-bench-template.csv to map trace fields -> bench driver inputs (attached).

Action items / owners:
- Alex/Jordan: send sample traces + answer clarifications above (Alex) — due Thu 2028-07-07 EOD
- Marissa (Redwood): propose bench configuration and expected metric dashboard — will share Tue 2028-07-06
- Dylan (Redwood): capture autoscaling suggestion and any fallback model variants for graceful degradation.
- Sean (me): schedule bench once traces are in and coordinate stakeholder invites.

Attachments: lumina_sample_traces.ndjson (sample), redwood-bench-template.csv, initial slo-mapping-proposal.pdf

Thanks — looking forward to validating numbers in a live replay.

–Sean
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

On Wed, Jul 5, 2028 at 9:12 AM Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks for a productive call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared plan for the performance qualification:
> 
> Summary of SLA targets you mentioned on the call:
> - E2E latency (95th) for interactive streaming chat: <= 200 ms
> - Steady-state QPS: ~120 requests/sec
> - Typical tokens per request (avg): ~1,200 tokens
> - Sustained concurrency target: ~600 concurrent active sessions (streaming-enabled)
> - Short peaks: up to 4x steady-state for bursts lasting ~8–15s

Thanks Sean — adding some technical framing so the bench results map cleanly to the SLA: 

Bench recommendations / definitions:
- Concurrency windows: define both 'active streaming sessions' (clients with open SSE/websocket streams) and 'in-flight requests' (RPCs that require model forward). For your workload they will largely overlap but tool-calls can create spikes in in-flight RPCs.
- Measurement windows: report 1s, 10s, and 60s rolling windows for QPS and tokens/s. 95th E2E should be computed over 60s windows to avoid noise from microbursts.
- Streaming cadence: bench driver should drive chunk emission at 150–200ms intervals and measure per-chunk latency + aggregate completion latency. We will capture both 'first-chunk' and 'final-chunk' latencies.
- KV cache / prefix caching: if Lumina reuses prefixes across sessions we can leverage prefix cache to reduce per-request token compute — please indicate % of requests with repeated prefixes.

Suggested bench config (initial):
- Model: rwd-2.1-llama-compat (float16) + quantized variant for reserve fallback
- Batch policy: dynamic continuous batching with a 30ms coalescing window to balance latency and throughput
- Autoscale policy for bench: target 70–75% GPU utilization at steady-state, with policy to add 25% capacity within 10s for burst handling.

I’ll prepare a bench docket with the CSV mapping and expected dashboards (latency percentiles, chunk cadence histogram, tokens/sec heatmap). Will attach when ready.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Chen <alex@luminalabs.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Park <jordan.park@luminalabs.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-06T08:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Concurrency windows and E2E latency benchmarks — post-call follow-up

Thanks, Sean & Marissa — good notes. A few clarifications from our side and I attached a small sample trace (lumina_sample_traces.ndjson) and a short doc describing our front-end buffering behavior.

Answers:
- Streaming vs non-streaming: ~85% streaming (user-facing chat), 15% non-streaming (batch summarization).
- Average tokens/request: 1,150 tokens (median ~980).
- Client chunk cadence: clients expect first chunk within 150ms, then subsequent chunks roughly every 200ms while typing.
- Tool calls: ~22% of streaming requests result in a synchronous external API call that adds 300–800ms on average. Tool latency distribution included in trace metadata.
- Prefix reuse: about 12% of requests reuse recent prefixes (short-term repetition).

We can provide full traces by Thu EOD (2028-07-07). For bench schedule the 07/11 window works for our infra folks — please lock it and share dial-in.

Two asks from Lumina: 
1) Can Redwood include a run with model fallback enabled (quantized variant) to show graceful degradation path and cost delta?
2) Can you capture per-chunk jitter (stddev of chunk latency) and return that in the result CSV?

Attached: lumina_sample_traces.ndjson (attachment), client-buffering-notes.pdf (attachment). Drive link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1A2b_sample_trace_link

Regards,
Alex Chen
Head of Platform Engineering
Lumina Labs

Perfect — thanks for the fast turnaround and traces, Alex. Confirming next steps and who’s responsible: 

1) Bench confirmed: Mon 2028-07-11 10:00–14:00 PT. I’ll send calendar invites to the infra and product folks at Lumina and Redwood now.
2) Redwood will run two bench passes:
   - Pass A: steady-state replay at 120 QPS for 60 minutes to validate 95th <= 200ms (reporting 1s/10s/60s windows).
   - Pass B: burst/replay with scaled bursts to 480 QPS (4x) in 8–15s windows to validate autoscale policy and tail behavior.
   - Both passes will include model-fallback runs (rwd-2.1 float16 vs rwd-2.1-quant) as requested.
3) Metrics we’ll deliver: per-chunk first/final latency percentiles, chunk-jitter stddev, tokens/sec heatmap, autoscale event log, and cost delta between variants.
4) Deliverable timeline: initial bench report draft by Wed 2028-07-12 EOD, final report + run artifacts by Fri 2028-07-14.

Links: HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-3819

If that all looks good I’ll lock invites. Anything else you want in the initial run?

–Sean
